text: A job does work and can notify on its own completion. An alert is a separate, standalone trigger that fires on a specific error number, severity level, or performance condition — independent of whether a job was even involved.

Severity 19+ is the real threshold requiring immediate attention — resource exhaustion or data corruption. An operator is Agent's model of who gets notified: historically pagers, in practice today email or a webhook routed to Teams or Slack.

A job's own notify_level_email fires only when that specific job fails. A standalone alert fires on the error condition itself, regardless of whether any job was running. A production strategy wires both to the same operator.

Job-level notification covers the routine maintenance you scheduled; severity-based alerts cover what you didn't schedule but need to know anyway. Next up: a real troubleshooting flow when a job actually fails.
